sam: Heads-up: small policy tweak and a short rollout tomorrow 2026-04-10 10:00 UTC. Please read and flag blockers.

sam: Summary:
- Quiet window: 09:30-11:00 UTC.
- Change: reduce default autoscaler burst_limit from 25% -> 15% for builder pools to dampen noisy scaleups.
- Canary plan: 5% for 20m -> 25% for 40m -> full flip if healthy.
- Reason: observed transient OOMs when many small jobs cause aggressive burst scaling.

clare: Will this affect batch jobs or only interactive builders?

sam: Applies to builder pools (batch + interactive). Batch jobs will still scale but with lower burst amplitude; long-running large-batch jobs are unaffected by steady autoscale targets.

devops-bot: devops-bot: maintenance window scheduled: 2026-04-10T09:30:00Z - 2026-04-10T11:00:00Z  id: mw-2169009999

tori: For Dedicated clusters: no automatic change. Tenant owners must opt in. We should post an opt-in form for anyone who wants the new default.

sam: Agreed. I will add an opt-in link to the release note. Also drafting a short changelog blurb.

oncall: What are the health gates for the canary?

sam: Health gates:
- 5xx rate <= 0.1% over 5m
- p99 latency delta <= +12%
- OOM occurrences == 0 in builder hosts over 10m windows
If any gate fails revert to previous config.

release-czar: I will add this to the weekly changelog under "autoscaler" and send an org reminder at T-3h. Draft blurb: "Autoscaler: lower default burst_limit for builder pools to reduce OOM risk under rapid small-job growth; Dedicated tenants unaffected unless opted in."

clare: Rollback quick steps:
1) `rctl canary set --service=autoscaler-builder --percent=0`
2) `rctl config apply --file=autoscaler-prev.yaml`
3) `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets` if needed to reprovision hosts
I put the runbook here: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/autoscaler-burst-change

devops-bot: deploy-bot: staging canary scheduled: job id dpl-20260410-0920

tori: I can monitor host OOM logs and heap metrics during canary. Will post markers in thread: start, 20m-check, 60m-check, flip/revert.

sam: Thanks — if anything urgent pops up DM me. Otherwise we'll follow the quiet-window runbook and publish a short postmortem if we hit any regressions.
